subject: Coefficient of determination (R^2) for a LGCP

messages.author: 959bffbdb3ddae02
messages.subject: Coefficient of determination (R^2) for a LGCP
parts:
Hello there INLA people!

I hope you can help me. I have fitted a Log Gaussian Cox Process using INLA and I am not sure if I can calculate the coefficient of determination for this model or if this coefficient is only valid for a linear model. I would only calculate it for the observed data. What are your thoughs about it?

Thank you in advance!

Rafael

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Coefficient of determination (R^2) for a LGCP
parts:
Hi,
That expression is really meant only for ordinary regression problems (and even than isn’t necessarily very interpretable, but that’s a different story), and isn’t defined for an LGCP model where the observations are sets of points, not counts at a finite set of locations.

Now, one can look at related Poisson regression versions of the same problems, by discretised space and taking counts of points in bins, but it’s clear that the way the discretisation is chosen intrinsically determines the resulting value. Unless my quick derivations are incorrect, the resulting R2 value when splitting into finer and finer uniform grid boxes has a limiting value of zero, regardless of the data  and estimated model.  There may be related concepts that make more sense for LGCPs, but R2 itself isn’t really one of them.

Finn
